notes:
=== CONCEPT ===
AXFR (zone transfer) is a DNS mechanism for syncing entire zone data between primary/secondary nameservers. When allow-transfer is misconfigured to 'any', an attacker retrieves every record in the zone in a single query — complete internal topology in seconds.

=== WHAT IT REVEALS ===
Every A, MX, NS, TXT, CNAME record: domain controllers (dc1, dc2), VPN endpoint, workstations, WSUS server with internal IPs. A successful AXFR collapses the entire internal host discovery phase.

=== CHAINING ===
dig ns → identify all nameservers → attempt AXFR against each NS → collect all internal hostnames/IPs → feed to nmap for service enumeration → prioritize DCs, VPN, mail servers.

=== PREVALENCE ===
Still common in environments with legacy DNS configurations. Internal zones (e.g., internal.corp.com) are more likely to be misconfigured than external zones.
